source.title: Instance-Dependent Early Stopping for Adaptive Data Pruning
source.authors: Su-Qin Yuan; Runqi Lin; Felix Azian; Lei Feng; Bo Han; Gang Niu; Masashi Sugiyama; Tong-Liang Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the ICLR 2025 paper titled “Instance-Dependent Early Stopping for Adaptive Data Pruning”; this differs from the 2026 IEEE venue and identifier metadata.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy during IES training, which bears on whether training reaches zero error, but does not directly reproduce the claim’s training recipes or broad settings.
record.gate_note: The noisy-label experiments report test accuracy and backpropagation saved, not training classification error. Other reported accuracy results concern test or transfer performance. Cited prior work is not treated as this study’s result.
record.test_reason: Appendix H directly measures full-training-set classification accuracy for a CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 trained with SGD under instance-dependent data pruning, a new training setting bearing on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that IES reduces computation while maintaining predictive performance and transferability. Appendix H reports retained accuracy on early removed examples; exclusion is reversible, and these examples are re-included an average of 13.14 times.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests instance-dependent early stopping and sample exclusion from backpropagation, rather than comparing network size or the cited gradient-training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training epoch changes the reported full-set training accuracy; the full set and early removed subset have separate reported values.

fits_no_version.finding: The first 5% of examples selected for removal retain 99.98%–100.00% accuracy at the reported checkpoints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IES preserves accuracy on initially removed examples through reversible exclusion and possible re-inclusion.

record.problems: Training-accuracy evidence relevant to V1 is limited to one CIFAR-10 ResNet18 IES experiment; the paper does not report training error for its noisy-label experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure training classification error for the claim versions. The noisy-label tables report best accuracy and saved mini-batches, not training classification error.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random labels; model-size dependence; conventional early stopping and regularization comparisons; Adam training. Random initialization is not explicitly documented for the Appendix H experiment.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and additional student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization-dependent learning speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus its absence, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text identifies an ICLR 2025 paper, Instance-dependent Early Stopping, arXiv:2502.07547v1, rather than establishing the supplied IEEE DOI identity. Verdicts apply to that text. The epoch-50 result does not qualify the eventual-convergence claim. Noisy-label test accuracy and pruning-related sharpness reductions do not establish V1 interpolation or V5 stability-threshold behavior.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test random labels, smaller models, comparisons across model sizes, early stopping versus longer training, or the stated SGD/Adam recipe comparisons for training error. Its training-accuracy table is for one CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 IES setting.
